summary: Recorded the source-explained boundaries of the third finding. Two behaviours are now durable: (1) the Node wrapper closes its proposal channel only for the removal case, because the guard requires the local node's Progress entry to disappear while it was present - a demotion to learner keeps that entry and therefore leaves the channel open - and applying a change that adds the node back takes the okBefore=false path, so an addition never re-opens a channel a removal closed, leaving the leadership-change branch (measured in the receipt) as the only repair site; (2) Node.Propose cannot report this state as such: with a nil channel it waits on a select over that channel, the caller's context and the node's done channel, so it returns only ctx.Err() or ErrStopped - the same results an ordinary lost proposal or a stopped node produces - which is why a caller with a deadline cannot tell the closed channel from a lost proposal except through the node's status. The measured account is unchanged and still rests on receipt c53145c01ad94b449ca1c8b81fe8d7b4 with its controls (parsed index 1), premises and violated witness (index 4) and its restore comparisons (indices 5 and 6); counterevidence gained the demotion exclusion and the source point that the wrapper's own warning does not describe this case, and limitations now name the only remaining unmeasured item - whether a group larger than two voters reaches the same state, where a re-added node's Progress entry is recreated in a different position and the leader that removed it may not be the leader that re-adds it - which is also what the question's discriminator now carries. No new execution was requested.
